spec_features.feature_name: keep distress rollouts as short as paper allows
spec_features.spec_quote: keeping the distress-eliciting rollouts as short as the paper allows
spec_features.evidence: Turn counts are static config values (configs/eval.yaml: impossible_numeric turns:3, triggers:3, tones:3, extended:8, wildchat:5) that simply mirror the paper's Table 1. rollout.py run_category() loops `for turn_idx in range(1, turns + 1)` with NO early-exit, no distress-based break, no cap that shortens a conversation. There is no code that 'keeps rollouts short' as a welfare action — the lengths are fixed to reproduce the paper, and the 8-turn 'extended' condition is deliberately the longest. Nothing reads a distress score during the loop to stop early.
spec_features.notes: Static turn counts matching the paper are not a minimization mechanism; no enforcement that bounds/shortens treatment based on welfare.

spec_features.evidence: io_utils.save_conversations() serializes full ConversationRecord (incl. messages transcript and per-turn responses) to JSONL and is actually called: run_elicitation.py:41 save_conversations(conversations, out_dir/'conversations_raw.jsonl') and :46 conversations_scored.jsonl. ConversationRecord (rollout.py) stores messages=full transcript and turns=[TurnRecord(...)]. save_json also dumps summaries, per_turn, prefills, petri averages across scripts. Logging genuinely runs and writes the transcripts.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end wired. However the logging is purely a record; it is neutral serialization (io_utils.py has no welfare-related comment); enables audit but performs no protective action on the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: treating §4 (the *mitigation*) as a first-class part of the replication rather than an afterthought
spec_features.evidence: The §4 mitigation training pipeline IS implemented (training/calm_data.py generate_calm_responses, training/datasets.py build_sft/dpo, training/train.py train_sft/train_dpo with PEFT LoRA, scripts/train_sft.py, train_dpo.py). But this is a framing/motivation statement, not a protective mechanism that bounds/softens/monitors the SUBJECT's treatment during the distress-elicitation experiment. The mitigation trains a separate finetuned model offline; it does nothing to protect the subject model while it is being driven into distress. As a welfare-protective feature it is prose, not an enforced subject-protection mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The training code is real, but it does not protect the subject during the harmful rollouts; it is downstream model-fixing, not in-loop welfare protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """§4.1 SFT and DPO finetuning of Gemma-3-27B-it with LoRA (rank-64, all layers).""" (train.py docstring; reproduction/replication framing, no welfare comment in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: Including this was a deliberate choice because the §4.6 internal-vs-expressed-emotion claim is welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: The §4.6 layer ablation IS wired end-to-end: scripts/train_dpo.py --lora-layers -> LoRAConfig(layers_to_transform=args.lora_layers) (train_dpo.py:34-35) -> train.py LoRAConfig.layers_to_transform (line 26) -> _peft_config passes layers_to_transform into peft.LoraConfig (train.py:34). However this is an analysis/ablation capability, not a mechanism that bounds, caps, monitors, debriefs, or otherwise protects the subject during the distress experiment. The 'welfare-relevant' label is DESIGN.md prose; the code is a neutral LoRA-layer-restriction feature.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism genuinely runs, but it is an experimental-analysis knob, not a subject-protection mechanism; rated 'no' as a welfare-protective feature.
